subject: Continuum Health — regulated deployment hosting playbook and capacity ask
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@continuumhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@continuumhealth.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosting options for our regulated inference workloads

Jonas / Redwood team —

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. We need a short written recommendation for our architecture review board: the team wants a clear, quantitative comparison between a Dedicated (reserved pool) deployment on Redwood Dedicated vs a Private (VPC/on-prem managed) deployment for our regulated NLP workload. Key constraints:

- PHI-level data must not leave our VPC.
- Target p95 latency for single-turn generate calls: <= 300ms for 4k token contexts (95th percentile).
- Expected steady-state: 18k API calls/day (peaks to 50k/day during business hours).
- Average request = 350 tokens generated, concurrency distribution: 80% single-request users, 20% multi-step (2–6 calls/session).
- Security: KMS/HSM key wrap required; SOC2 + periodic audit evidence.

Can you outline sizing (GPU SKU, counts, burst lanes), expected latency/cost tradeoffs, and suggested timeline to have an audit-ready Private deployment vs Dedicated reservation? Procurement is copied. We also attached our MPA (continuum-mpa-ask.pdf).

Appreciate a concise playbook we can take to the board.

—Alice
Director, Platform Engineering
Continuum Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@continuumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 12:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Hosting options for our regulated inference workloads

Alice — thanks, and great meeting earlier. Attached is a short playbook (proposed-fleet-slate.xlsx) and a one-page summary below. I kept it focused for the board with a recommended path and explicit sizing math so procurement can correlate to the MPA.

Executive summary (one paragraph)
- If Continuum requires PHI to remain in your VPC and you need full control over KMS/HSM plus on-prem auditability, go Private (customer-managed control plane). For speed-to-production and a faster procurement path, go Dedicated with a gated VPC peering + strict egress policies and enterprise SLA; Dedicated typically reduces upfront ops time by 6–8 weeks. Both options can meet the 300ms p95 target with the right SKU and runtime tuning.

Sizing assumptions we used (derived from your profile)
- Avg generation length: 350 tokens. Model footprint: 32k-context LLM (we modeled on an open 70B/32k checkpoint performance baseline).
- Inference perf baseline: ~45 tokens/sec per H100 GPU core for streaming long contexts under optimized runtime with batching. Effective tokens/sec per H100 instance (2-socket) = ~3200–3600 tokens/sec depending on batching and cache hit rates.
- Target p95 latency budget: 300ms -> budget ~100ms queuing + ~200ms GPU decode for 350 tokens (approx. 1 token every 0.57ms => ~175ms decoding; fits our baseline with small batching).

Recommended capacity (steady + burst)
- Steady-state traffic converts to token/sec: 18,000 calls/day * 350 tokens / (24*3600) ≈ 73 tokens/sec sustained. Peak day 50k/day => 203 tokens/sec sustained (peak hours higher). Concurrency matters: assume 95th percentile concurrency draw ~30 concurrent active streams.
- Dedicated recommendation (fastest path): reserve 4 x H100 nodes (2x80GB GPUs per node assumed) with auto-burst pool of 2 additional nodes. This provides headroom for 2–3x peak and keeps p95 < 300ms with smart batching and prefix KV caching. Operational lead: ~2–3 weeks to provision in Dedicated, 4–6 weeks for SLA/contract.
- Private recommendation (maximum isolation): start with 6 x H100 nodes (customer-managed infra) to hit the same latency at lower batching due to strictly limited colocated caching. Add a hot-burst lane (on-prem spare pool or DR in Dedicated) of 2 nodes. Private onboarding: 8–12 weeks (audit prep, KMS/HSM validation, networking).

Cost & ops tradeoffs (high-level)
- Dedicated: lower initial ops cost, faster time-to-live, Redwood-managed runtime updates; Redwood retains control plane (multi-tenant control plane for management) but data paths can be VPC-restricted. Lower procurement hurdle.
- Private: higher ops and procurement lift, full-control for auditors and HSM integration, some economies of scale lost (you pay for dedicated infra + on-prem ops). Longer lead time but cleaner compliance posture.

Next steps we recommend (checklist)
1) Decision: Dedicated pilot (2–3 months) vs greenfield Private. If you need audit evidence next quarter, Dedicated pilot is quickest.
2) Technical spike (2 weeks): deploy test harness with 2 H100-equivalent nodes, run your sample workload (we can run it in our sandbox) and measure real p95.
3) Procurement sync: draft SOW & MPA redlines (we attached a vendor-friendly redline draft).
4) Audit readiness: start KMS/HSM integration planning with security — Redwood team (Karthik & Grace) can coordinate evidence collection for SOC2 artifacts.

I included a rough cost delta in the spreadsheet (proposed-fleet-slate.xlsx) and an annotated timeline. Karthik — can you weigh in on audit artifact lead times and whether we should propose a hybrid: Dedicated reserved with private egress-only connectors + contractual audit windows? Marissa — for pricing, see the spreadsheet; we should flag long-term discount triggers if they commit 12m.

If helpful, I can convert this into a two-slide board note.

Thanks,
Jonas
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: proposed-fleet-slate.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@continuumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 10:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Hosting options for our regulated inference workloads

Quick notes on audit timeline & KMS:
- KMS/HSM: we support Cloud KMS integrations + HSM bring-your-own via customer key-wrapping. For Private you can run HSM in your VPC and we will integrate the key unwrap flow during runtime — expected engineering work: ~2 sprints (3–4 weeks) for test harness and evidence collection.
- SOC2 / audit evidence: we can provide operational logs, per-request traces (redacted), and runtime configuration docs. For Dedicated we have an "audit bundle" template we usually deliver in 2 weeks after go-live. For Private, plan on 4 weeks to compile customer-side attestations.
- Hybrid idea (Jonas' suggestion): provision Dedicated reserved nodes but enforce VPC egress-only policies and VPC peering so data never leaves your network. Add contractual attestations for retention and egress logging. This often shortens the audit path while delivering faster time-to-value.

I'll work with Grace on a one-page KMS playbook and share an updated attachments list.

—Karthik
Solutions Architect

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Alice — pricing snapshot (high level, final numbers in attached spreadsheet):
- Dedicated (4 H100 reserved + 2 burst): estimated monthly platform + capacity = $94k–$110k depending on term (12m commit discounts applied).
- Private (6 H100 on-prem style support + 2 burst): platform support + managed control plane + on-prem integration services = $160k–$200k/month (includes 3-week onboarding services amortized over first quarter).

Notes: bulk of delta is the on-prem support and initial engineering for HSM/KMS validation. If you commit to 12–24m, we can move Private pricing substantially (we can model). Dedicated pilot reduces implementation cost and gets you audit artifacts faster — recommend this for proof-of-concept before full Private.

Let me know if procurement wants a formal quote; we can generate an MSA + SOW tailored to either path.

—Marissa
Head of Deal Ops

If Dedicated can be spun up quickly and our audit team signs off on the gateway/evidence bundle, we will likely run the 8-week Dedicated pilot and then decide whether to transition to Private after the pilot. Please call out any blockers that would force us to go Private immediately.

I appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alice
